qs.q: A physiological experiment measures the response of beta-3 adrenergic receptors located on adipocytes. What is the primary metabolic response mediated by these receptors?
o: Stimulates storage of glycogen in cells
Suppresses uptake of glucose by adipocytes
Enhances breakdown of lipids within fat cells
Decreases production of heat in the body
Encourages synthesis of new lipid molecules
qs.e: Beta-3 adrenergic receptors on fat cells stimulate lipolysis and thermogenesis via cyclic AMP pathways.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Neurophysiology I Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which autonomic substance demonstrates equal affinity for activating both alpha and beta adrenergic receptors?
qs.e: Epinephrine exhibits equal potency and affinity for both alpha and beta adrenergic receptors. Norepinephrine shows a notably stronger affinity for alpha receptors compared to beta receptors.

qs.q: A 65-year-old man is evaluated for lower urinary tract symptoms caused by benign prostatic hyperplasia. His physician initiates therapy with an alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist. What is the primary physiological mechanism of this medication class?
o: Suppressing pituitary release of luteinizing hormone
Inhibiting the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
Relaxing smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder neck
Inducing apoptosis of epithelial cells in the transition zone
qs.e: Alpha-1 antagonists relieve dynamic lower urinary tract obstruction by relaxing smooth muscle tone in the prostate and bladder neck. Inhibiting testosterone conversion is the mechanism of 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors rather than alpha-blockers.
qs.s: Male Reproductive Pathology: Comprehensive Review: MCQs

qs.q: What is the main physiological response mediated by beta-3 adrenergic receptors found on fat cells?
qs.e: Fat cells predominantly feature beta-3 adrenergic receptors which mediate lipolysis. Beta-1 and beta-2 receptors control heart muscle and bronchial muscle functions respectively.

qs.q: Which substance activates alpha and beta adrenergic receptors most nearly equally?
qs.e: Epinephrine activates both alpha and beta adrenergic receptors. Norepinephrine has relatively greater activity at alpha receptors and beta-1 receptors than at beta-2 receptors.
Alpha-1 receptors are located on vascular smooth muscle and cause contraction (vasoconstriction) when stimulated.

qs.q: Beta-1 adrenergic receptors are located primarily in the:
qs.e: Beta-1 receptors increase heart rate (chronotropy) and contractility (inotropy).

qs.q: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor stimulation leads to:
qs.e: Beta-2 receptors cause relaxation of smooth muscles in the bronchioles and blood vessels of skeletal muscle.
